title: Image Processing and Analysis of VPS13D Recruitment to Mitochondria
author: Marianna Leonzino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bvgnn3ve

steps.title: Build Kymographs
steps.instruction: Build kymographs by tracing a line ROI across the mitochondria that was illuminated with Blue Light.

steps.title: Measure Intensity Profiles
steps.instruction: Measure the intensity profile and background for the mitochondrial signal.

substeps.instruction: Trace a line ROI across the center of the mitochondrial signal on the kymograph to measure the intensity profile.
Take a background profile using the same line ROI outside the illumination area.

steps.title: Normalize Fluorescence Intensities
steps.instruction: Normalize the fluorescence intensities to the min and max values using the formula: Normalized f[t] = (f[t] - f min [t]) / (f max [t] - f min [t]), where f[t] = F mito [t] - F bkgd [t].

steps.title: Define Cell ROIs
steps.instruction: Analyze cells coexpressing VPS13D^EGFP and mitoBFP individually and store each cell outline as an ROI in the Fiji ROI Manager.

steps.title: Preprocess MitoBFP Channel
steps.instruction: Apply the 'Gaussian Blur' and 'Enhance Local Contrast' tools to the MitoBFP channel to average brightness and clarify mitochondrial shape and margins.

steps.title: Quantify VPS13D^EGFP Recruitment
steps.instruction: Use an automated Fiji macro to measure VPS13D^EGFP signal overlapping with mitochondria and signal localized in the surrounding cytosol.

substeps.instruction: Run the provided macro to automate the splitting of channels, Gaussian Blur (sigma=2), and CLAHE (blocksize=127, histogram=256, maximum=3) for mitochondrial mask generation.
Use the macro to calculate the intensity of VPS13D^EGFP on mitochondria and in the surrounding cytosol.
Calculate the ratio between the intensity of VPS13D^EGFP on mitochondria and the intensity of VPS13D^EGFP in the surrounding cytosol for each cell.
Plot a graph indicating the enrichment of VPS13D^EGFP on mitochondria.
